transcript.text: Shark NZ801UK anti hair wrap upright - suction has gone really weak over the last couple of weeks, barely picks up crumbs. Have emptied the bin. Any ideas before I buy a new one?

Switch it off and unplug it (or take the battery off) first. It is probably not time to buy a new one yet. Weak suction on upright vacuums like the Shark NZ801UK is rarely a motor failure; it is usually an airflow restriction. The next most likely culprits are clogged filters or a blockage further down the line. Filters in these models trap fine dust and can become choked over time, especially if they haven't been washed recently. Additionally, hair or debris can get stuck in the hose or floorhead. 1. Check the filters: Locate the pre-motor filter (usually near where you empty the bin) and the HEPA filter (often at the top rear). If they look dirty, wash them in cold water only. Crucially, let them dry for at least 24 hours before putting them back. A damp filter will severely restrict airflow.
2. Check for blockages: Detach the hose from the main unit and look through it. Shine a torch down if needed. Also check the wand and the neck of the floorhead where it connects to the machine. Ensure nothing is stuck inside. Let me know if you found any blockages or if the filters were dirty/damp.
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — Lost suction is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage in the hose, tube or floor head — check and clear those before suspecting the motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]

Hose is clear, a coin drops straight through and I can't see any splits. Wand is clear too. Never washed the filters, didn't know they were there. The felt one is caked with fine dust. Will wash them now.

That makes sense; if you've never washed them, they are likely choked with fine dust which acts like a solid wall to airflow. Please ensure they dry for at least 24 hours in a warm, airy spot. Putting them back damp will kill suction just as much as dirt does. While those are drying, please turn the floorhead over and check the brush bar (roller). On upright vacuums like this, hair and threads often wrap tightly around it, preventing it from spinning or restricting airflow at the base. Cut away any debris with scissors if needed, and make sure the roller spins freely by hand. Let me know how the suction is then.
Brushroll had a bit of fluff, nothing major, and it spins freely. I washed the foam and felt filters and left them 24 hours. Suction is back to like new now, massive difference.

That is excellent news. It sounds like the clogged filters were most likely the culprit; washing them has restored the airflow and brought your suction back to normal. To keep it running well, try to wash those filters every month or two, depending on how often you use it. Just remember they must be completely dry (24 hours) before you put them back in, otherwise the dampness will choke the suction again. You shouldn't need a new vacuum just yet. Is there anything else I can help you with today?
